# Decision output

## Recommendation

**Action:** contribute

**Summary:** Contribute a small fix or docs PR to an existing ETL toolkit instead of starting a new framework.

## Why you

You already shipped Python ETL and a FastAPI service, so a focused upstream contribution is credible evidence for data engineering.

## Why now

Six hours/week for two weeks fits one well-scoped PR better than a greenfield framework.

## Existing alternatives

Mature ETL toolkits already cover batch orchestration basics.

## The gap

Your gap is evidenced collaboration on a real codebase, not another personal toolkit.

## First experiment

Spend 45 minutes reproducing the upstream quickstart and filing notes on one sharp edge in onboarding.

## Success condition

Continue to a PR only if you can point to a concrete docs bug or failing quickstart step.

## Capability unlocked

Open-source contribution evidence plus deeper pipeline design reading.

## Downstream paths

- portfolio writeup of the contribution
- maintainer relationship
- stronger data-engineering interviews

## Trade-off

Less ownership theater; more dependency on upstream review speed.

## Alternative

If you needed income immediately, offer a short freelance ETL cleanup for a local SME using your SQL/Python skills.

## Confidence

- **Known:** profile skills, time budget, saturated framework space for beginners' “new ETL”.
- **Inferred:** contribution path beats greenfield for trajectory signal.
- **Unknown:** which upstream repo is healthiest this month without a fresh search.
